tiling-kagome.note: the kagome tiling alone: edges and vertices, no beat

tiling-truncated-trihex.note: the truncated-trihex tiling alone: edges and vertices, no beat

tiling-snub-trihex.note: the snub-trihex tiling alone: edges and vertices, no beat

tiling-truncated-square.note: the truncated-square tiling alone: edges and vertices, no beat

tiling-truncated-hex.note: the truncated-hex tiling alone: edges and vertices, no beat

tiling-rhombitrihex.note: the rhombitrihex tiling alone: edges and vertices, no beat

tiling-snub-square.note: the snub-square tiling alone: edges and vertices, no beat

tiling-elongated-triangular.note: the elongated-triangular tiling alone: edges and vertices, no beat

tiling-kagome-filled.note: kagome with the faces inked inward — the hexagons clear the inset and the triangles do not, which is what makes one tiling look unlike another

tiling-octagon-pair-filled.note: two filled truncated-square tilings at 6 degrees — the moire of the faces, not of hairlines

grid-hex-filled.note: fill on a closed-form grid: the honeycomb inked inward, no catalogue table involved

tiling-kagome-twist-contours.note: two kagome tilings at 5 degrees — a catalogue tiling is a lattice, so the twist machinery applies unchanged

tiling-octagon-ring-envelope.note: the truncated-square tiling against a ring family — a tiling beats a scalar like any lattice

lines-pair.note: two line families at 4°, plain composite

lines-pair-envelope.note: the same pair enveloped: broad diagonal fringes, carrier gone

lines-pair-contours.note: contours at integer D over the envelope

lines-pair-ratio.note: the heterodyne ratio map of the pair

lines-pair-mask.note: envelope with the regime mask most of the way up

lines-trio-contours.note: three families at 0/3/9° — the third joins the character scan

rings-pair-envelope.note: two ring families off-centre: the two-centre fringe system

rings-pair-contours.note: the character-hills skeleton: contours of D between ring centres

rings-pair-contours-zoom2.note: the same skeleton at scene zoom 2 — guards the capture framing math

squares-pair-contours.note: square rings at a 10° twist — piecewise index fields with corners

hexrot-spiral-envelope.note: two concentric-hexagon families, one rotating 0.02 rad per ring — past the fold radius spacing/θ = 300 the family branches, and the phase trio must report adjacent branches, not index neighbours (the sector-hash bug)

radial-pair-contours.note: two radial fans off-centre — the sector-count scalar under contours

line-ring-contours.note: mixed classes: a line family against a ring family

rings-sum-handover.note: equal-pitch rings — the sum eye must fade into the ray fan seamlessly

fan-trio-envelope.note: three dense fans — marginal station winners must not deviate the sweep

walk-pair-envelope.note: two walking circle families — schedule boundaries must not stipple

pitch-3to1-envelope.note: lines at 3:1 pitch — the (3,-1) fringe must survive the average

pitch-3to1-contours.note: lines at 3:1 pitch — contours must draw the (3,-1) skeleton

pitch-3to1-ratio.note: lines at 3:1 pitch — the map must darken along the (3,-1) beat

pitch-5to2-envelope.note: lines at 5:2 pitch — the (5,-2) fringe must survive the average

rings-3to1-ratio.note: offset ring families at 3:1 — the map structure is per-pixel reduction

wave-pair-envelope.note: two wave families at 5° — bent index fields enveloped

spiral-ring-envelope.note: a spiral against rings — unequal index gradients everywhere

counter-spirals-render.note: Archimedean spirals of opposite handedness — the pitch SIGN is the chirality (both twins once dropped it through abs), and a counter pair beats in M_A + M_B rays where a same-handed pair beats in M_A - M_B

logspiral-pair-render.note: the loxodromic clock: two log-spiral families, counter-handed — self-similar arms whose member gap grows with radius, so the beat rosette is scale-free

georings-envelope.note: the dilation clock: two geometrically spaced ring families (log spiral at bend 0) about displaced centres, enveloped — hyperbolae-like fringes in log-radius

line-field-envelope.note: a Gaussian-warped line family against a plain twin, enveloped

line-fork-render.note: theta/tau at amount 5 — the charge-5 fork grating, plain render

line-fork-envelope.note: the fork pair enveloped — five fringes ending at the defect

line-field-contours.note: the warped pair under contours — level sets of the field itself

grid-twist-envelope.note: the square-lattice twist pair — both slow characters survive the sweep

grid-twist-contours.note: contours on the twist pair — the class the first lattice-contours bug hid in

grid-hex-twist-contours.note: hex lattices at 3° — three families, two generators, under contours

grid-tri-line-contours.note: a triangle lattice against a scalar partner — the line family is set parallel to a lattice edge family (pitch (√3/2)·16 ≈ 13.86 at 30°) so a real slow beat exists for the contour channel to draw

grid-trio-twist-contours.note: three square lattices at 0/2.5/5° — the third joins the lockstep sweep

grid-field-envelope.note: the dipole-field grid pair from the bug report, enveloped

grid-field-contours.note: the same pair under contours — the fix that seeded this zoo

single-ring-envelope.note: one scalar family alone — the A == B envelope fallback

single-grid-envelope.note: one lattice alone — the sweep washes it to its cell mean

grid-lines-ratio.note: ratio view over a grid and two scalars — the ranking must skip the grid

grid-ring-ratio.note: the eta map of a ring family over a square lattice — dark lobes where a grid family matches the local ring direction and pitch; the measurement reads lattice ink families, so one scalar plus a lattice is a map

grid-twist-ratio.note: the eta map of a square-lattice twist pair — matched dual-ring families beat slowly everywhere, so the map reads uniformly deep in the fringe regime

walk-field-quilt.note: identical walking ring pair, one dipole-warped, below 2 px per member — no sum pockets

dutynull-linear-envelope.note: 2:1 line pair at coarse duty 1/2 — the station is null and the linear envelope flat

dutynull-square-envelope.note: the same pair under a square-law observer — the null reopens on the ramps
